Long Description: Lips puckered as if kissing, then blowing outward (often with hand motion). Accompanied by smiling eyes or a playful head tilt.
Leaning in to kiss one or both cheeks, often with puckered lips and a smile.
One corner of the mouth raised (unilateral sneer), often with a slight head tilt back and narrowed eyes.
Eyes rotated upward or to the side, often combined with a slight head tilt or exasperated expression. Conveys contempt or boredom.
Quick raise and lower of the eyebrows, often as a subtle non-verbal hello.
Brief, partial lowering of eyebrows or corrugator muscle activity, creating small vertical wrinkles between brows.
One or both hands covering the face (palm on forehead/eyes), often with head lowered or shaking slightly. Exaggerated slap motion is common.
Palm slapping the forehead, often followed by a head shake or eye roll.
Eyebrows pulled together and downward, mouth corners turned down, often with forehead wrinkles.
Mouth twisted or teeth bared slightly, often with wrinkled nose and squinted eyes.
Repeated up-and-down tilting of the head, often with a neutral or positive facial expression.
Side-to-side turning of the head, frequently with a furrowed brow or firm mouth.
Head angled to one side, often with softened eyes or a slight smile.
Mouth opened wide with relaxed jaw, often combined with widened eyes and raised eyebrows.
Lower (or upper) lip held gently between teeth, often with a slight head tilt, softened eyes, or focused gaze.
Lips pressed firmly together and inward (disappearing lips), indicating hidden negative feelings like anger, fear, or disagreement.
Lips pressed tightly together and slightly pushed forward, often with a furrowed brow.
Thumb and index finger forming an 'L' shape placed against the forehead. Often accompanied by a smirk or eye roll.
Brief lowering and drawing together of eyebrows (furrowed brow), slight lip tightening or pressing, and narrowed eyes. Fleeting tension in the jaw or lower eyelids.
Very brief one-sided mouth raise or smirk (unilateral lip corner pull), often with a slight eye narrowing or head tilt.
Quick nose wrinkle, upper lip curl or raise, and slight squint. Can be isolated to the nose/mouth area.
Quick raising and drawing together of eyebrows (inner corners up), widened eyes with tense lower lids, and slight mouth opening or lip stretching.
Fleeting Duchenne smile markers: slight eye crinkling (crow's feet) and cheek raise, even if the mouth smile is suppressed.
Brief inner eyebrow raise with downturned mouth corners, drooping eyelids, or slight chin quiver. Often limited to the eye region.
Rapid raising of eyebrows with forehead wrinkles and brief eye widening. Mouth may open slightly in a quick 'O' shape.
Mouth open wide and slack (jaw dropped), typically paired with widened eyes and raised eyebrows.
Mouth formed into a rounded 'O' shape, typically with widened eyes.
Nose scrunched upward with furrowed brows and slightly raised upper lip.
Lips pushed forward and upward (protruding), often with downturned mouth corners and sad or pleading eyes.
Lips tightly puckered and pushed forward (as if tasting something sour), often with a wrinkled nose and squinted eyes.
Eyebrows lifted high, creating forehead wrinkles, often with widened eyes.
Shoulders raised briefly combined with raised eyebrows, open palms (if visible), and a slight head tilt or downturned mouth.
Only the left eyebrow arched upward while the right remains neutral or lowered, often with a slight head tilt and neutral-to-slightly-smirking mouth.
Only the right eyebrow arched upward while the left remains neutral or lowered, often with a slight head tilt and neutral-to-slightly-smirking mouth.
Mouth corners turned upward, often with crinkled eyes (crow's feet) and raised cheeks. Can be genuine (Duchenne smile involving eyes) or polite.
One-sided smile with one mouth corner raised, often with a slight eye squint or eyebrow raise.
Eyes narrowed, often with furrowed brows and a slight head tilt forward.
Tongue extended straight out from the center of the mouth, often with a neutral or cheeky facial expression.

Short Description: Disgust, grossed-out reaction, or childish rejection.
Long Description: Tongue extended straight out with a scrunched nose, squinted eyes, and often a slight head tilt back.
Tongue protruding to one side of the mouth, frequently paired with a wink, smile, or concentrated eyes.
Tongue extended and moving side-to-side or wiggling, usually with a mischievous grin or squinted eyes.
Eyes opened maximally, showing more sclera (whites), often paired with raised eyebrows and open mouth.
One eye closed briefly while the other remains open, often with a slight smile or head tilt.
